sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Rocket ATM walks a factory-fresh Genmega G2500 from error code 0030 to online. In key management, enter the default secure password of six zeros twice, then assign two new six-digit codes (the demo uses all ones and all twos), let the 30-second countdown finish without cutting power, and confirm the EPP state change to move from maintenance into operation mode [gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:00:42]. Operator functions open with 555555. Under customer setup, confirm surcharge mode is enabled, because a disabled setting means the machine never charges anyone, set the surcharge owner name, and raise the default $1.50 surcharge, which the demo sets to $3 [gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:04:02]. Processor settings go to SSL pass-through for internet communication, Standard 3, seven bits even parity, reversal on host error enabled, TLS 1.2 with hostname verification, Gen DCC and Visa DCC enabled, the Standard 3 options set enable, enable, disable, disable, and EMV with all AIDs enabled. For Columbus Data, host setup takes routing ID CDSA0, host IP 208.35.209.1 and port 6965 on both lines, with configuration set to scheduled [gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:16:29]. ATM Connect adds the physical side: every Genmega ships with the same default vault code, 123456 then pound, plus universal keys for the chest door and the top [ujDLOkqXvfg @ 00:03:46].

Anthony of ATM Connect puts real numbers on vault cash using three of his own locations. The first ran 327 transactions, dispensed $22,000 and produced $1,100 in total profit, needing at least $5,500 a week; the second ran 283 transactions, dispensed $17,000 for $990 profit and needs $4,200 a week; the third ran 350 transactions, dispensed $25,000 for $700 profit and needs $6,200 a week, so the three together demand a minimum of $16,000 just to stay in service [kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:10:13]. He pegs the average surcharge at $3, which means a $40,000 automation package needs 13,333 transactions to pay back [kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:13:55]. Webb converts the cash load into vaulter terms: the industry standard pays a vaulter between 70 cents and $1.25 per transaction depending on volume, and his lesson from a vaulter who loaded only $500 twice a week is to require $3,000 per load and immediate refills when the machine hits a $200 or $100 threshold [6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:03:50]. He separates level one service, meaning bill jams, paper jams and cash-outs covered by the base deal, from repairs like dispenser failures, broken keypads, screen replacements, reprogramming and software upgrades, which the ATM owner should pay the vaulter extra to handle [zHPWp60QbG4 @ 00:04:14].

For dispensaries, Webb's build is specific. Under the new sponsor-bank guidelines the operator loads only their own cash, never mixing it with dispensary money, fills out the rules package through the ISO to the sponsor bank, and discloses where the dispensaries are, how much cash goes in and what commission is paid; he suggests an off-the-record conversation with the local bank first to take their temperature [ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:05:35]. The hardware spec is a new machine with a 2K cassette, ideally two for 4K because the location needs a lot of money, and possibly a second ATM so one failure does not leave the owner blowing up the operator's phone [ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:07:10]. Velocity Merchant Services describes the cashless alternative: point-of-banking runs an ATM-style card withdrawal inside the POS, prints a voucher receipt instead of cash, works in increments of 10, 20, 50 up to 1,000, and settles in change, so a $17.20 sale runs as $20 with $2.80 handed back, with the fee paid by merchant or cardholder [uBEewd90EL8 @ 00:02:22]. Megalith's Open Receive skips approval entirely, taking Bitcoin or USDT and USDC through a receive-only NWC code with no reserve, no cut and no chargebacks, installed on their own WooCommerce store by a coding agent [lnoavHYKfcI @ 00:02:57].

callout.title: Bench-Tested Moves From the Operators
callout.body: Small checks that separate a machine that earns from one that becomes a paperweight or a lost location.
items: Before buying any used machine, get the model number, manufacture date and software version, confirm the seller has both passwords and the combo, then run it past your processing company before paying [ATMDepot - Make Money with ATM Machines — ETBd5FI2JHY @ 00:02:28].

Check the tip indicator before signing for delivery; metallic silver means it was not tipped, and transport the ATM with its back on the truck bed and the front facing the sky [ATM Connect — ujDLOkqXvfg @ 00:00:13].
Set the ATM clock to current time because processors look at transaction timing, and turn on Spanish alongside English where customers need it [Rocket ATM — gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:12:21].

Write a lead clause into the vaulter deal so new locations the vaulter hears about become yours, paid as a lead fee, before the vaulter cuts you out with their own machine [Philip Webb — 6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:06:54].

sop_steps.title: Source a compliant machine
sop_steps.action: Buy a Genmega G2500, Onyx, Hyosung Halo 2 or Force from an authorized distributor or processing company.
sop_steps.detail: Reject anything without an EMV reader, secure-connection software or TLS 1.2, and treat refurbished units as acceptable only with at least a 90-day or six-month warranty [ATMDepot - Make Money with ATM Machines — ETBd5FI2JHY @ 00:02:45].

sop_steps.title: Unbox, open and power up
sop_steps.action: Inspect the tip indicator, open the vault with 123456 then pound, untwist the shipping wires and power on.
sop_steps.detail: Keep the black rodent caps in every cable hole, swapping the flat cap and the pass-through cap to whichever side the outlet sits on [ATM Connect — ujDLOkqXvfg @ 00:05:06].

sop_steps.title: Program surcharge, processor and host
sop_steps.action: Reset key management passwords, enable surcharge, set SSL pass-through with TLS 1.2, enable EMV, then enter terminal number, routing ID and host IP and port.
sop_steps.detail: Finish with a cassette total to test the printer and add cash, where ten bills registering as $200 confirms a $20 denomination, then call the office for the key management information [Rocket ATM — gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:22:19].

sop_steps.title: Fund the vault and lock in service
sop_steps.action: Load cash sized to real weekly dispense, not $1,000, and sign a vaulter agreement if someone else loads it.
sop_steps.detail: Size loads from history, with Anthony's locations needing $4,200 to $6,200 a week, and require vaulters to load $3,000 at a time and refill at a $200 or $100 threshold [ATM Connect — kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:10:30] [Philip Webb — 6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:03:50].

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: Hardware loyalty splits the operator bench. Chad Otsuji has owned both brands and calls Genmega the clear winner: their first Genmega ran four years without a single jam or error, while one Hyosung placed an hour and a half from home failed the same day it went live, came back broken two days after the fix, and forced three or four round trips before Otsuji sold it [6zaxeyp07Zg @ 00:00:40]. Otsuji adds that owners in their Facebook group report jam after jam on Hyosung units, and that an email landed flagging Hyosung machines as prone to jackpotting, where hackers drain the cash with no reimbursement [6zaxeyp07Zg @ 00:02:41]. Weigh that against the fact that Genmega is the only brand Otsuji's site sells. ATMDepot draws the line by model rather than badge: the Genmega G2500, Hyosung Halo 2, Genmega Onyx and Hyosung Force sit on its good list, while the Triton 9600, Genmega G1900, Hyosung 1800 CE, Tranax and most old bank ATMs land on the avoid list as too old, too bulky or not upgradeable [ETBd5FI2JHY @ 00:03:14]. The working read: buy the specific model, verify EMV, TLS 1.2 and current software, and treat brand-wide verdicts as one operator's route history.

Vault cashing is where Philip Webb argues both sides on camera. In one video Webb tells operators not to become vault cashers at all, because filling someone else's machines for 70 cents to $1.25 per transaction while carrying the service calls and fronting your own cash just swaps one nine-to-five for another [oIqtdUU2Qtg @ 00:00:33]. In the same breath Webb admits PDQ did it anyway, and lays out the alternate playbook: take a vault route in a new city to buy credibility, build relationships with the store owners, prospect new bars, convenience stores and gas stations while you are already driving there, and then either cut the owner loose or buy their portfolio [oIqtdUU2Qtg @ 00:01:45]. From the owner's side of the deal, Webb prefers a vaulter over an armored car because it runs a little cheaper, and armored crews usually show up next day or two days after a service call [zHPWp60QbG4 @ 00:01:15]. Anthony of ATM Connect pushes the other direction: hiring a third-party company to load your ATMs significantly decreases profits you are already splitting with the business owner [kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:11:22]. Net: outsourced vaulting buys reach and coverage, the margin pays for it, so run the per-transaction math first.

High-risk and cash-heavy merchants get two competing playbooks. For dispensaries, Velocity Merchant Services pushes the cashless ATM, or point of banking: the card runs like a withdrawal through the POS, a receipt acts as the voucher, amounts round to increments such as $20, and the clerk hands back change, so on $17.20 the customer selects $20 and gets $2.80 back [uBEewd90EL8 @ 00:02:22]. Philip Webb runs the physical-cash play instead: sponsor banks now allow dispensary placements if the ATM owner loads their own cash and never mixes it with dispensary money, armored carriers will not service it, and splits run from 60 to the operator down to 50/50 [ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:02:19]. For card-not-present high-risk sellers, Megalith lays Durango's 1.95 to 4.95 percent plus a 5 to 10 percent rolling reserve held 90 to 180 days against Open Receive, a free Bitcoin and stablecoin rail with no approval and no chargebacks that runs beside a card account rather than replacing it [lnoavHYKfcI @ 00:01:28]. Merchant Maverick's top pick, Payment Nerds, publishes a flat 2.99 percent plus 3 cents, which the reviewer calls almost unheard of in high-risk processing, while Durango keeps pricing undisclosed with long contracts [2E0M95jxJpU @ 00:04:01].

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive failures on the route are empty machines and missed service. Philip Webb hired a vaulter who loaded $500 on Monday, ran dry Monday night, and did not return until Friday, leaving the ATM down two or three days at a stretch; when confronted, the vaulter insisted they loaded thousands, but the journals showed $500 in and $500 out [6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:03:06]. Webb's fix is written into the agreement: a minimum load of $2,000, really $3,000, and an immediate refill when the balance hits the $200 or $100 threshold, plus defined response windows from one hour out to two days, with penalties when the vaulter misses them [6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:03:50]. Distance compounds every failure: Chad Otsuji's Hyosung sat an hour and a half away, worked for a day or two after each fix, and burned three or four round trips before being sold off and replaced [6zaxeyp07Zg @ 00:01:41]. Webb's dispensary advice reads like a scar from the same problem: place a new unit with a 2K cassette, or two for 4K because the location needs a lot of money, and consider a second ATM so one going down does not leave the owner blowing up your phone [ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:07:10].

The economics trap is underfunding and overpaying. Anthony of ATM Connect pulls three of their own locations: 327 transactions dispensing $22,000 for $1,100 profit needs at least $5,500 a week, 283 transactions dispensing $17,000 for $990 needs $4,200, and 350 transactions dispensing $25,000 for $700 needs $6,200, so the three together need a minimum of $16,000 in vault cash [kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:10:13]. That shreds the guru line of filling each machine with $1,000, since at an $80 to $100 average withdrawal the box empties fast. Anthony also flags a $40,000 ten-machine automation package promising 24,000 to 48,000 in year one; at a $3 average surcharge it takes 13,333 transactions just to recover the buy-in, and one buyer posted 77 approved withdrawals in three months, about $144, on a barbershop placement with $1 going to the merchant and no contract [kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:14:11]. Philip Webb lived the small-scale version: a hotel vault deal on a $4 surcharge paying $1.50 per transaction produced 40 to 50 transactions a month, about $40 to $60, for two or three trips, and the location could not be sold, so it carried no intrinsic value [YgQxm2IWnKw @ 00:02:06].

Security and banking relationships are the tail risks. WKRN News 2 filmed a four-man crew at a Reliant Bank parking lot at 2:15 in the morning pry the outer layer with heavy crowbars in 30 seconds, hook tow chains from a stolen Ford F-250 to the half-inch safe door, rip the unit off its pedestal, and leave with more than $20,000 in under two minutes [DzLysrdcerg @ 00:00:45]. On the dispensary side, Philip Webb describes years of operators running ATMs under fictitious names like a plant shop or an auto body store, paying commissions in cash or by check; when caught, the sponsor bank shut it down, the ATM came out, and it went right back in under a new name [ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:05:06]. The above-board path now means reporting locations, cash and commissions to the ISO and possibly the local bank, which puts your whole banking relationship at stake. Webb also warns that a vaulter servicing a location for years can take the owner's referrals and cut you out of the next deal, so lead ownership belongs in the agreement [6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:06:21]. ATMDepot closes the gate: a felony or financial crime on your record means you cannot legally run an ATM business [Cb9qwLOH7y0 @ 00:02:08].

callout.title: Lock These Down Before Cash Goes In The Box
callout.body: Every gate below comes from a loss, a fired vaulter, or a dead machine that a named operator lived through on their own route.
items: Put the vaulter's minimum fill level, refill threshold, service response time, and penalties in a signed agreement before they touch your machine [Philip Webb — 6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:04:05].
Add a clause that any location leads the vaulter picks up from your merchant belong to you, with a paid referral if you want, so they cannot cut you out [Philip Webb — 6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:06:54].
Reconcile every vaulted ATM against your settlement deposits daily and monthly, because a vault casher can move your money with a click of a mouse [Philip Webb — zHPWp60QbG4 @ 00:06:39].

On any used machine, get the model number, manufacture date, software version, both passwords and the combo, then clear it with your processor before paying [ATMDepot - Make Money with ATM Machines — ETBd5FI2JHY @ 00:02:28].

chapters.pull_quote: We don't get in this business to get a job, we get in this business to leave our job. — Philip Webb (YgQxm2IWnKw @ 00:02:45)
action_checklist: Program the surcharge before going live: confirm surcharge mode is enabled, enter the owner name, set the amount to $3.00, and accept with Enter [Rocket ATM — gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:05:32].
Set communication to SSL pass-through with TLS 1.2, enable EMV and all AIDs, and set the clock to current time because processors look at transaction timing [Rocket ATM — gS2sjD2NYOU @ 00:10:29].

On delivery, check the tip indicator is still silver before signing, transport the unit lying on its back, and keep the black hole caps in so rodents cannot chew the wires [ATM Connect — ujDLOkqXvfg @ 00:00:00].
Size vault cash from real dispense history: divide monthly dollars dispensed by four weeks to get the minimum weekly cash each location needs [ATM Connect — kXEFZM-F90k @ 00:10:30].
Price any vaulter deal against volume, budgeting the industry standard of 70 cents to $1.25 per transaction so it pays both you and the vaulter [Philip Webb — 6k0qIHsvs0M @ 00:05:06].

Before chasing a dispensary placement, have an off-the-record conversation with your local bank to take their temperature so you do not lose the whole banking relationship [Philip Webb — ZN0dj7u6nmo @ 00:06:04].
